findings.description: Most severe: the REAL production seam that would carry out SHEET-TAB-002 is a stub. `ViewSheetsAdapter::set_tab_order` in adapters.rs (lines ~240-246) unconditionally returns `Ok(())` and never calls `self.api` (the underlying `SheetsApi` primitive) — it does not issue any Sheets `batchUpdate`/`updateSheetProperties` call. Only the in-memory test fake (`InMemorySheetsView::set_tab_order` in testkit.rs) actually records/mutates an order, which is why `tabs.rs`'s `republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order` test passes despite production doing nothing. This is itself a B-direction instability: B3 correctly names `ViewSheetsAdapter::set_tab_order` and states it 'SHALL NOT invoke the underlying SheetsApi primitive'; B2's SHEET-ORDER-012 asserts the opposite ('the real (runtime) client is the one that issues an actual updateSheetProperties/batchUpdate metadata call') — factually wrong per the code; B1 stays silent on the production adapter entirely, only describing the testkit fake.

The real EARS text names exactly three macro-groups ('views → config → event logs'), but the code's actual canonical order (`workbook_tab_order()` in lib.rs) inserts a fourth, unstated group — History (owned by `reports`) — positioned between views and config: `[Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax, History, Tax Rules, Residency, Platforms & Aliases, Ledger Events, Tax Events]`. All three B reconstructions independently pin this exact insertion (B1 SHEET-ORDER-004, B2 SHEET-ORDER-004, B3's 'History SHALL immediately follow the Tax view'). None of the three A sketches include a History/reports group at all — unsurprising, since nothing in the given EARS text hints at it — so this whole group is pure code-side surplus the compressed spec omits.

The spec speaks only at the macro-group level ('views', 'config', 'event logs'); the real code pins the exact tab names and exact intra-group sequence as a literal constant list (Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax; Tax Rules, Residency, Platforms & Aliases; Ledger Events, Tax Events) with zero classification/sorting logic — `workbook_tab_order()` is a hardcoded `Vec<&'static str>`. All three B runs reconstruct this identical 10-name literal sequence. All three A runs, by contrast, explicitly flag in their own Assumptions sections that intra-group order (and any concrete tab identity beyond 'Positions') is unspecified by the EARS text, and invent a generic stable/tie-break-by-current-index rule instead of the real fixed names — confirming the spec genuinely leaves this open, which the code then resolves via a plain constant rather than any computed policy.

Both directions converge on the same clause ('reasserting the order idempotently on republish') with opposite readings. All 3 A sketches interpret 'idempotently' as requiring a diff/minimal-move mechanism: compute current vs. desired index per tab and emit move-operations ONLY for tabs not already in place (empty op list when already correct) — explicitly justified by A1/A2 as satisfying 'idempotently' via a no-op-when-unchanged design. The real `Publisher::republish` does no such diffing: `let order = workbook_tab_order(); if self.client.set_tab_order(&order).is_err() { ... }` runs unconditionally on EVERY republish call with the complete fixed list, regardless of which tabs were touched that cycle or whether the order already matched — confirmed identically by all three B reconstructions (e.g. B2 SHEET-ORDER-009: 'unconditionally and idempotently, regardless of which subset of tabs was passed'; B1 SHEET-ORDER-007: 'regardless of how many/which tabs were included'). The real 'idempotent' is referential (same deterministic result every call), not change-minimizing — a genuine, verifiable mismatch anchored on the same spec word from both directions.

The EARS text says nothing about failure or lock semantics around the ordering operation, but the code (and all 3 B reconstructions, in close agreement) pin specific unwanted-behavior rules: a failed lock-acquire skips BOTH `batch_update_view` and `set_tab_order` for that cycle entirely (no partial writes), returns `published: false`, and leaves `stale_tabs` unchanged; a `set_tab_order` failure alone sets `published: false` but never appends anything to `stale_tabs` (which accrues only from per-tab `batch_update_view` failures — see `republish`'s `all_ok` handling in lib.rs). None of the A sketches touch lock acquisition, `RepublishOutcome`, or stale-tab bookkeeping at all — this entire error-semantics layer is pure code-side surplus relative to the compressed spec text.

Minor B-internal instability: the Tax tab's reserve-summary band (`TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary"`) is explicitly documented in lib.rs as part of the Tax surface and NOT a fifth entry in the ordered list. B2 and B3 both surface this exclusion as an explicit requirement bullet; B1 omits it entirely from its numbered list. No A sketch addresses it (expected, since the compressed EARS text gives no hint of a Tax sub-range).

notes: Real code read directly: crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (workbook_tab_order() as a hardcoded 10-entry Vec, Publisher::republish's unconditional full set_tab_order call, RepublishOutcome/stale-tab handling), crates/sheets-view/src/testkit.rs (InMemorySheetsView::set_tab_order as the only implementation that actually records order + fault injection via set_order_fails), crates/sheets-view/tests/tabs.rs (workbook_order_views_then_config_then_logs_positions_landing and republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order tests, which assert against the exact fixed 10-tab constant), and crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs (ViewSheetsAdapter::set_tab_order — the production no-op). Overall the B direction is extremely convergent on the substantive reconstructed requirement (the literal 10-tab order, the unconditional full reassert, the lock/failure semantics) — the two internal disagreements (production-adapter behavior in B2 vs B3; Reserve Summary exclusion present in B2/B3, absent in B1) are narrow and don't threaten the classification. The A direction is highly convergent structurally (TabGroup-style enum, Views<Config<EventLogs ordering, diff-based idempotency, unspecified-intra-group-order self-flagged as invented) with only minor variance (A3 makes Positions its own top-level group rather than a tiebreak within Views; A1 alone hard-errors on a missing Positions tab while A2/A3 explicitly decline to). Per the classification rubric, most of the A-side inventions (tab classification mechanism, missing-Positions handling, intra-group tiebreak) are self-admitted assumption artifacts with no textual basis and are NOT counted as findings; the one A-side item promoted to a finding (the diff/minimal-move idempotency mechanism) is anchored directly to the explicit spec word 'idempotently' and is real, verifiable behavior absent from the code, which is why the overall call is BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY-DRIFT — though the volume and severity of drift is overwhelmingly on the B (code-side surplus) side, culminating in the production set_tab_order no-op, which looks like an actual unimplemented-feature bug relative to SHEET-TAB-002's intent, not just a documentation gap.
